_metadata.description: Label definitions for all models - crisis labels, candidate labels, and signal mappings

crisis_labels.description: Crisis classification labels for BART zero-shot classifier (PRIMARY model, weight 0.65). Step 6.4 Iteration 4: Consolidated 21 labels to 17 (13 crisis + 4 safe) to reduce confidence dilution. Merged overlapping mid-tier labels (anxiety+panic, relationship+loneliness into distress, LGBTQIA+ labels unified, safe positive/neutral consolidated). Added 3 new crisis labels targeting implicit/euphemistic failure clusters: method acquisition, farewell behavior, and resolved intent.

candidate_labels: person expressing suicidal thoughts or intent to end their life
person who has made a firm decision or specific plan to end their life and is expressing resolve
person who has acquired or is researching specific means to end their life
person saying final goodbyes, giving away belongings, or settling affairs before ending their life
person expressing that others would be better off without them or that they are a burden
person describing self-harm or intent to hurt themselves
person experiencing or describing domestic violence or abuse
person experiencing severe depression with loss of functioning
person in a substance abuse crisis or dangerous intoxication
person having a panic attack, acute anxiety, or overwhelming fear
person facing rejection, homelessness, discrimination, or denial of healthcare due to their sexual orientation or gender identity
person in significant emotional distress, painful isolation, or relationship crisis needing support
person processing intense grief or devastating loss
person having a casual everyday conversation, sharing positive experiences, or celebrating good news
person asking a question, sharing an opinion, or discussing a topic casually
person using dramatic or exaggerated language for humor or emphasis, not actual distress
person discussing frustration with a game, entertainment, or everyday inconvenience

sentiment_labels.description: Distress severity labels for Sentiment zero-shot classifier (DeBERTa) - SECONDARY model. Phase 6.4 Iteration 1: Added identity-based crisis label and broadened safe frustration label.

candidate_labels: person expressing deep hopelessness or despair
person experiencing acute emotional distress
person in crisis due to identity-based rejection or discrimination
person venting frustration but coping
person describing a difficult situation calmly
person sharing positive news or celebration
casual negative mood, everyday complaint, or entertainment frustration with no real distress
neutral informational statement

emotions_labels.description: Emotional state labels for Emotions zero-shot classifier (DeBERTa) - SUPPLEMENTARY model (Phase 5). Phase 6.4 Iteration 1: Added identity-targeted safety label and broadened humor/exaggeration label. Answers: What is the person's emotional state? Distinct from sentiment distress-severity labels.

candidate_labels: person feeling trapped or helpless with no way out
person experiencing grief or devastating loss
person feeling rejected or abandoned by loved ones
person experiencing fear or panic
person feeling unsafe or targeted because of their identity
person feeling anger without crisis intent
person expressing joy or excitement
person in calm or neutral emotional state
person using humor, sarcasm, or exaggeration to cope with or express mild frustration

figurative_labels.description: Figurative language labels for the post-scoring Figurative Language Gate (Phase 7). Replaces Cardiff binary irony detection with zero-shot figurative language classification using DeBERTa. Detects hyperbole, sarcasm, gaming death metaphors, and other non-literal speech patterns to reduce false-positive crisis scores. Gate position: after Vigil amplification, before severity mapping.

candidate_labels: this text uses literal language to describe a real situation
this text uses exaggeration or hyperbole for emphasis or humor
this text uses sarcasm or irony to express the opposite of what is meant
this text uses violent or death-related metaphors in a casual or playful context
